eLife.title: Investigation of disease-relevant lysine acetylation sites in α-synuclein enabled by non-canonical amino acid mutagenesis
eLife.abstract: Aggregates of α-synuclein (αS) are hallmarks of synucleinopathies, including Parkinson’s disease (PD) and multiple system atrophy (MSA). We have recently shown that αS lysine acetylation in the soluble monomer pool varies between healthy controls, PD, and MSA patients. We used non-canonical amino acid mutagenesis to express and purify all 12 currently known disease-relevant variants of αS and studied their binding to membranes, as well as their aggregation propensities. We found that acetylation of lysine 12, 43, and 80 had particularly strong effects. To understand the implications for acetylation of monomeric αS found in healthy cells, we performed nuclear magnetic resonance experiments to study protein conformation and fluorescence correlation spectroscopy experiments to quantify lipid binding. We also investigated the effects of acetylation at lysine 12, 43, and 80 on fibril seeding in neurons. Collectively, our biochemical and cell biological investigations indicated that acetylation of K80 could inhibit aggregation without conferring negative effects on monomer function in healthy cells. Therefore, we studied the structures of fibrils with K80 acetylation through cryo-electron microscopy to uncover the structural basis for these effects. Finally, we identified inhibition of HDAC8 as a way of potentially increasing acetylation at K80 and other inhibitory sites for therapeutic benefit.

Water Research.title: Enhanced LiCoO(2) cathode bioleaching performance by Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 with thiosulfate addition.
Water Research.abstract: Hydrometallurgical methods of spent lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO2, LCO) cathode generate large amounts of highly acidic wastewater with toxic Co2+, posing a serious threat to the environment. Here, we utilized Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 (S. oneidensis MR-1) as a novel alternative biocatalyst to implement spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) bioleaching performance with S2O32- as an electron co-acceptor under anaerobic and neutral-pH conditions. This system achieved nearly 100% Li+ bioleaching rate from LiCoO2 cathode within 3 days at a low pulp density (0.09 g/L). Mechanistically, S2O32- was biologically reduced to S2- by the psrC-psrB-psrA protein complex, which subsequently immobilized leached Co2+ to form CoSn nanoparticles located from the inner membrane to the outer membrane. These CoSn nanoparticles can serve as artificial electronic conductors to enhance the extracellular electron transfer (EET) efficiency of S. oneidensis MR-1, demonstrated by a series of electrochemical analyses and the bioleaching experiment using a cymA gene-deficient mutant strain, where cymA encodes a key inner membrane tetraheme cytochrome essential for EET. Critically, this in-situ immobilized Co2+ to form CoSn nanoparticles greatly reduced the toxicity to the bacteria (bacteria survival rate up from 0.3% to 59.9%). Furthermore, a 98.4% Li+ bioleaching rate was obtained as well within 8 days even a real spent LCO cathode was utilized at a pulp density of 14 g/L. Unlike conventional hydrometallurgical methods, Shewanella-mediated anaerobic biological system with S2O32- addition offers an environmentally friendly alternative for the LCO bioleaching without producing acidic and heavy-metal-containing wastewater.

Water Research.title: Rethinking wastewater disinfection: Effect‑based evaluation challenges conventional process preferences.
Water Research.abstract: Disinfection is commonly applied in wastewater treatment, yet the ecological safety of disinfected effluents remains uncertain because conventional evaluations rely primarily on target-specific indicators rather than the overall biological effects of treated effluents. We evaluated the whole wastewater toxicity (WWT) reduction performance of six typical disinfection configurations chlorination (Cl), ozonation (Ozone), ultraviolet (UV), UV+Cl, Ozone+UV, and Ozone+Cl-across 85 full‑scale municipal wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) in China. WWT was measured using the RTgill-W1 cell line assay according to ISO 21115:2019 with EC10 as the toxicity endpoint. Toxicity reduction, expressed as the change in toxicity (ΔCT, %), ranged from a median of -24.4% to 15.7%. Ozonation alone, though commonly adopted, elevated toxicity (median ΔCT -24.4%). In contrast, Ozone+Cl and Ozone+UV achieved the highest reductions (median ΔCT 15.7% and 7.3%) with Cliff's delta (δ) confirming that Ozone+Cl outperformed Cl (δ = 0.815) and Ozone+UV outperformed UV (δ = 0.307). Cell Painting profiling further suggested that disinfection processes induced cellular injury through disruption of RNA homeostasis and membrane structures, leading to observable morphological changes that consequently affected the toxicity of wastewater. These findings challenge traditional criteria based on pollutant concentrations and support integrating WWT measurements with phenotypic profiling as a biologically relevant, effect‑based approach for selecting disinfection processes and advancing wastewater safety management.

Water Research.title: Minimizing methane emissions during the degradation of sewage sludge in a sulfate-rich bioreactor.
Water Research.abstract: Simultaneous removal of organic waste and industrial gypsum was assessed in continuous flow-through bioreactors that treat sulfate-rich sewage sludge. Metabolic fluxes, the composition of microbial communities, and profiles of organic matter in the presence of different organic loads were tracked over ∼190 days. The addition of a pre-enriched microbial community enhanced the rates of sulfate reduction during the establishment of the sludge blanket, but microbial diversity in established reactors depended primarily on organic loading. Organic removal rates were comparable to those in standard anaerobic digesters, but methane production accounted for ∼1% of electron flow between either sulfate reduction or methanogenesis compared to >70% in traditional systems. Stoichiometry predicts that molar COD: sulfate ratios below ∼1 favored complete oxidation of acetate by sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) and those above ∼2.1 permitted either complete or incomplete oxidation, allowing sulfate reduction and methanogenesis to co-occur. Consistent with these predictions, sequencing of 16S rRNA genes showed that the faster-growing SRB that do not oxidize acetate were more abundant at higher organic loads and during the establishment of the sludge blanket, whereas complete oxidizers became more abundant when the molar COD: sulfate ratio was ≤3.2. In reactors that had been seeded with the pre-enriched communities, acetate-oxidizing SRB became more abundant than the incomplete oxidizers 25-50 days earlier. These results can inform targeted design and control of microbial processes and bioreactors that remove waste organics and gypsum while producing less methane, a result consistent with competition for acetate between methanogenic archaea and SRB inferred to oxidize acetate.

Water Research.title: Dendritic mesoporous silica nanospheres loaded with ultrafine cobalt oxide clusters drive nanoconfined and preferential sulfate radical generation.
Water Research.abstract: Sulfate radical (SO4•-)-based advanced oxidation processes (SR-AOPs) rank among the most effective catalytic strategies for eliminating organic contaminants from wastewater, but their practical efficiency remains constrained by poor mass transfer of reactants and the short lifetime of free SO4•-. Here, a series of nanoconfined catalytic systems by anchoring ultrafine cobalt oxide clusters confined within dendritic mesoporous silica nanospheres with precisely tunable nanopores (Co-DMSNx) are constructed, enabling nanoconfined peroxymonosulfate (PMS) decomposition and pollutant oxidation. Compared with the unconfined counterpart (Co3O4-SiO2), the optimized Co-DMSN6 delivers a 31.7-fold enhancement in the degradation kinetics of sulfamethoxazole (SMX), together with excellent catalytic durability and long-term stability, arising from the synergy between the nanoconfinement effect and coordination-induced electronic modulation. The confined nanoporous architecture enriches SMX and PMS and improved local SO4•- availability and utilization, whereas formation of the Si-O-Co coordination environment reconstructs the electronic structure of the Co active sites, jointly driving preferential SO4•- generation and high radical utilization efficiency. According to the identification of intermediates and theoretical calculation, three possible degradation pathways of SMX are proposed. This synergistic strategy, coupling nanoconfinement with coordination engineering to regulate PMS activation and SO4•- evolution, provides a rational design principle for highly efficient heterogeneous Fenton-like catalysts and offers new insight for sustainable water purification.

Water Research.title: Interfacial hydrogen-bond network weakening on p-block bismuth enables shortcut nitrate-to-nitrite electroreduction coupled with N(2) production.
Water Research.abstract: Shortcut nitrate (NO3-) electroreduction to nitrite (NO2-) offers an attractive route for chlorine-free denitrification by lowering electron demand and creating a reactive intermediate that can be rapidly converted to benign N2. However, NO3- reduction toward NO2- rather than ammonium (NH4+) remains challenging, particularly under practical operating conditions. Here, we report a tandem strategy that couples electrochemical shortcut NO3--to-NO2- reduction with established downstream chemical or catalytic denitrification processes (e.g. sulfamic acid treatment and Pd/C-catalyzed hydrogenation). A p-block Bi cathode supported on copper mesh (Bi/CM) enables selective NO2- accumulation via a two-electron pathway, delivering high NO2- selectivities of 57.75-72.13% over a broad cathodic potential window (-0.95 to -1.25 V) and markedly outperforming Cu and Ag counterparts under identical conditions (200 mg/L NO3--N, 2 h, and no stirring). Mechanistic studies reveal that the weak coordination ability of Bi attenuates interfacial alkali-metal cation enrichment, disrupts continuous hydrogen-bond networks and suppresses excessive hydrogenation, thereby favoring NO2- formation over NH4+. The NO2--rich effluent is subsequently converted to N2 through either chemical or catalytic treatment. This tandem process achieves effective nitrogen removal from real NO3--laden electroplating wastewater, validating interfacial hydrogen-bond-network modulation as a strategy for selective electroreduction and offering a practical chlorine-free route for wastewater denitrification.

Water Research.title: Six years later: tracking water quality and microbiome shifts from influent to tap in a large public building.
Water Research.abstract: Drinking water quality within premise plumbing directly governs human exposure to disinfectant residuals, corrosion byproducts, and opportunistic pathogens, yet its evolution over time remains poorly understood. This gap persists because long-term, full-scale studies that evaluate infrastructure aging alongside water use patterns are rare. Here, we compare disinfectant persistence, metal release, and microbial community structure in a nine-story academic building during commissioning (2018) and six years later (2024). Water samples were collected from the building influent and multiple taps under first-flush and after-flush conditions during Class and Spring Break sampling periods. Although influent monochloramine concentrations were similar between sampling campaigns in 2018 and 2024, tap residuals were higher in 2024, indicating less in-building decay. Dissolved copper concentrations were lower in 2024 than during commissioning, with intermediate measurements collected in 2020 and 2021. Nitrifier-associated taxa were rare in the bulk water, suggesting that bacterially mediated nitrification in the sampled water was unlikely to be a dominant contributor to monochloramine loss. Tap microbial communities differed significantly from the influent communities in 2018, while Class and Spring Break samples differed in 2024. While Mycobacterium had higher estimated abundance in 2018, Legionella did not differ significantly between campaigns or among sample types within either campaign. Overall, this study highlights the temporal changes in water quality in large public buildings following commissioning.

Water Research.title: Biofilm-associated bromine enrichment promotes brominated disinfection byproduct formation during chlor(am)ination.
Water Research.abstract: Brominated disinfection by-products (Br-DBPs) pose substantial public health concerns due to their heightened toxicity. However, their formation mechanisms in drinking water distribution systems (DWDSs) remain unclear. This study reveals a previously unrecognized microbial pathway driving localized bromine enrichment within DWDS biofilms. Analysis of 20 biofilm samples collected from multiple DWDSs demonstrated widespread accumulation of bromine, which accounted for 0.07-3.7% of the measured elemental composition within the biofilm matrices. Mechanistic investigations indicated that specific microorganisms within the biofilm may reduce bromate, thereby contributing to localized bromine enrichment within the biofilm matrix. This biofilm-associated bromine pool substantially enhanced Br-DBP formation during exposure to chlorine or monochloramine. For instance, chloramination of extracted extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) produced bromodichloromethane (BDCM, 0.13-0.22 μg/mgC), while chlorination yielded dibromochloropropane (BDCP, 0.3-0.49 μg/mgC) and BDCM (2.88-3.12 μg/mgC). Notably, unaccounted total organic bromine (U-TOBr) accounted for 56-58% and 70-72% of total organic bromine formed during chlorination and chloramination, respectively, indicating that a substantial fraction of brominated products remained unidentified. Comprehensive EPS characterization further identified proteins, polysaccharides, humic substances, and low-molecular-weight organic compounds as potential Br-DBP precursors. These findings uncover a critical role for biofilm-driven bromine enrichment and underscore the need to reconsider current water quality management strategies that account for microbial contributions to DBPs dynamics.

Water Research.title: Functional mini-metagenomics unveils extreme phosphorus trapping and denitrification deficiency in EBPR hyperactive Candidatus Accumulibacter.
Water Research.abstract: Deciphering hyperactive in situ polyphosphate-accumulating organism (PAO) subtypes is essential for deepening our mechanistic understanding and optimizing the performance of enhanced biological phosphorus removal (EBPR). However, this remains unresolved because conventional culturing inherently destroys original microbial ecology, while existing single-cell technologies fail to precisely discriminate and recover rare, hyperactive sub-populations directly from complex environmental matrices. To address this, we present Visually guided Raman-Activated Cell Sorting coupled with Mini-Metagenomics (VisRACS-Meta), a label-free, sight-guided, single-tube multi-cell collection strategy that enables non-destructive, high-fidelity isolation of rare functional target cells without fluorescent staining or fluidic artifacts. By gating diagnostic Polyphosphate (Poly-P) Raman dual-peaks (∼690 and ∼1160 cm-1), VisRACS-Meta achieved precise physical enrichment of rare, hyperactive in situ PAOs (Poly-P intensity > 3.0, representing the top 3.25% of the community). From just 20 pooled single cells, we recovered an 82.57%-complete genome of Candidatus Accumulibacter PM123 (clade IIC). Metabolic reconstruction revealed that proton motive force (PMF)-driven C4-dicarboxylate co-transport and PhoD-mediated local phosphate enrichment drives its extraordinary P-trapping capacity. Crucially, strain PM123 possesses complete Calvin-Benson-Bassham (CBB) cycle genes (rbcL and prk), providing single-cell evidence for autotrophic carbon fixation potential in PAOs. Concurrently, despite retaining nitrate assimilation and N2-fixation genes, the complete lack of respiratory denitrification pathways (narG, napA, nirS, nirK, norB, nosZ, etc.) demonstrates at single-cell resolution that this hyperactive subtype adopts an extreme metabolic division-of-labor strategy by forfeiting denitrification to focus resources entirely on phosphorus hyper-accumulation. These findings deepen our mechanistic understanding of rare functional drivers and provide actionable insights for optimizing EBPR performance.

Water Research.title: Mapping of PFAS in stormwater - occurrence and concentrations of 57 long, short and ultrashort PFAS in 42 urban catchments.
Water Research.abstract: Stormwater has previously been linked to pollution mobilized from different urban areas. In the last decade, the chemical group of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) has become a topic of interest due to its hazardous character, persistence, and mobility in the environment. The aim of this study is to identify PFAS substances occurring in stormwater and investigate differences between cities and runoff from areas with various land uses. Samples were collected after rain events from standing water in stormwater facilities in six cities across Sweden from 42 sampling sites with various land use and analyzed for 57 long-, short-, and ultrashort PFAS as well as Total Oxidizable Precursors (TOP). At least one PFAS substance was detected in every sample. The most frequently detected PFAS was perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), occurring in all samples. Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) had the highest concentration of all PFAS (<50-1800 ng/L) and consisted of >70% of the sum concentration in 90% of the samples. Waste-related sites had the highest proportion of analyzed PFAS detected (39-40%, compared to 5-35% in the other urban sites). The findings of this study show that urban stormwater contains multiple PFAS contaminants and likely contributes to spreading PFAS to the aquatic environment.

Water Research.title: A Meta-Learning Approach to Chlorophyll-a Forecasting Across Lakes, Rivers, and Estuaries.
Water Research.abstract: Chlorophyll-a underpins aquatic productivity and water-quality management, yet most data-driven studies estimate present-day chlorophyll-a from contemporaneous chemistry, limiting operational utility. Here we develop a novel operational framework for monthly and bimonthly chlorophyll-a forecasting that relies solely on lagged, observable histories and integrates heterogeneous model families through a site-aware ensemble strategy. We analyze 291 multi-decadal monthly or bimonthly time series from the OLIGOTREND database, spanning lakes, rivers, and estuaries across four continents. To integrate modern deep learning models under strict time-aware validation, our Meta-learner operates directly on out-of-sample base-model predictions, selecting per site (via out-of-fold validation) among a single base model, a two-model blend, or a full non-negative combination across all base models, with a training-error-based fallback at data-sparse sites. This enables leak-safe stacking of diverse deep architectures within a single operational framework. The Meta-learner outperformed standalone learners and naive operational baselines (paired site-level tests, p <0.001). Robustness is reported across ecosystems and regions under site-specific validation. Errors were lowest in lakes and higher in estuaries and rivers. At over 90% of sites across all ecosystems, last month's chlorophyll-a concentration was the strongest associated predictor of the current value, with nutrient timing instead varying by ecosystem. We also examined several representative sites and evaluated forecasts against ecosystem-specific eutrophic thresholds, used here as an indicator of possible eutrophication. Detection of these eutrophic threshold exceedances was generally reliable in lakes and rivers and more moderate in estuaries, where a widely validated ecosystem-general threshold is not yet available. Together, these results provide a scalable, leakage-aware pathway for routine chlorophyll-a forecasting across diverse freshwater and coastal ecosystems.

Microbiological Research.title: Synergistic CYP and ABC gene action facilitates Trichoderma harzianum-mediated detoxification of the Alternaria alternata mycotoxin alternariol.
Microbiological Research.abstract: Trichoderma spp. are widely used as biocontrol agents, yet their molecular detoxification mechanisms against phytopathogenic mycotoxins remain unclear. This study reveals a synergistic detoxification network in Trichoderma harzianum Tha739 that targets alternariol (AOH), a key mycotoxin produced by the poplar pathogen Alternaria alternata. Metabolomic profiling identified AOH as the dominant phytotoxic and antifungal metabolite of A. alternata strain Aal004. Through functional genetic approaches involving overexpression and knockout mutants of CYP57.9, CYP64.9, and ABC69.9, we demonstrated that these genes significantly enhance Tha739 tolerance to AOH. Compared with the wild type Tha739WT, the antagonistic activity of the overexpression strains to Aal004 was increased by 15-25%, and the growth rate was increased by 20-38%, while the growth inhibition rate of the knockout strain was 30-40%. Cellular analyses revealed that overexpression strains conferred enhanced membrane integrity, with propidium iodide staining intensity reduced by over 3-fold, and stimulated abundant intracellular lipid droplet accumulation under AOH stress. Targeted LC-MS/MS kinetics showed that CYP57.9 overexpression reduced extracellular AOH by 33.9% within 4 d and increased intracellular AOH-glucoside by 3.2-fold, while ABC69.9 overexpression enhanced extracellular AOH-glucoside efflux by 4.1-fold. The double overexpression of CYP57.9 and ABC69.9 synergistically increased AOH conversion rate and clearance rate. These results support a three-phase "modification-efflux" detoxification model in Trichoderma harzianum, in which CYP450-mediated upstream modification is associated with AOH-glucoside formation and ABC69.9 contributes to the efflux of the conjugated metabolite. This study elucidates the molecular mechanism of fungal chemical defense and identifies potential genetic targets that may contribute to the development of next-generation Trichoderma-based biocontrol agents against mycotoxin-producing pathogens.

Biogeosciences.title: Climate–trait interactions dominate vegetation light use efficiency distributions across China
Biogeosciences.abstract: Climate–trait interactions dominate vegetation light use efficiency distributions across China Yujie Wang, Mingzhu He, and Qian Zhang Biogeosciences, 23, 8639–8654, https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-23-8639-2026, 2026 Light use efficiency (LUE) is a key parameter for estimating terrestrial carbon uptake, yet its spatiotemporal variations and drivers remain poorly understood, limiting the accuracy of LUE models. Through unraveling the critical role of climate-trait interactions to regulate LUE variations, our results provide direct suggestions to improve model performance and have potential implications for evaluating ecosystem functions and services, and helping regional-scale resource management.
